PullRequest.Title: chat: Clean up stale marketplace plugin records
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

- verify that a recorded plugin target still exists as a directory before reporting the marketplace resource as installed
- watch marketplace plugin target parents so external target deletion refreshes discovery and transitions the installation record to Missing
- centralize exact-URI plugin uninstall in `IPluginInstallService`, removing raw `installed.json` entries even when marketplace metadata cannot hydrate
- clean metadata, enablement, source caches, and the marketplace installation record without touching a same-name plugin
- cover production-path deletion, reload, unhydrated entries, stale uninstall, and shared-source cleanup with focused regression tests

Fixes #338584.

- Passed: `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/plugins/pluginInstallService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/pluginInstallService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/plugins/agentPluginServiceImpl.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/plugins/pluginInstallService.test.ts`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The diff explicitly changes the removable marketplace plugin callback from launching cleanup without awaiting it to returning uninstallPlugin(), and uninstallPlugin awaits cleanupPluginSource. The traced UI callers await plugin.remove(), while cleanupPluginSource performs concrete filesystem existence checks, recursive deletion, and parent pruning. Only the exact duration and affected cache size vary by installation.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem stats and recursive deletion of cloned repositories or npm/pip cache trees
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added wait grows with the number and size of files in the plugin source cache (especially git repositories and package-manager trees) plus the number of parent directories pruned.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: User-visible uninstall latency now includes the full cache cleanup, leaving uninstall actions and marketplace state pending for the duration of recursive filesystem work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery removed the durable installed entry, launched cleanupPluginSource(...).catch(...) without awaiting it, and returned true immediately, so repository cleanup ran off the uninstall interaction's critical path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new centralized uninstallPlugin removes the entry and then awaits cleanupPluginSource before resolving; both the plugin action and customization marketplace await that promise.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `await this._pluginRepositoryService.cleanupPluginSource(...)` at RIGHT line 77 replaces the deleted MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery code that invoked `cleanupPluginSource(...).catch(...)` without awaiting before `return true`.
Findings.Title: Keep cache deletion off the uninstall critical path
Findings.Impact: Uninstalling a GitHub/Git URL/npm/pip plugin with a large cached repository or dependency tree can now keep the UI in its "Uninstalling" state for seconds while recursive deletion completes, whereas the same action previously completed after updating the installed record.
Findings.Evidence: RIGHT line 77 awaits AgentPluginRepositoryService.cleanupPluginSource. That method calls fileService.exists(cleanupDir), fileService.del(cleanupDir, { recursive: true }), then serially resolves/deletes empty parents. MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery now returns uninstallPlugin from its remove callback, UninstallPluginAction returns plugin.remove(), and CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService awaits plugin.remove(); therefore this filesystem cleanup is directly on both user-visible uninstall paths.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve uninstall after the durable entry is removed, and launch best-effort source cleanup in the background with the existing logged error handling; if cleanup completion must be observable, expose it separately rather than blocking the uninstall action.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold start or reload with marketplace plugins installed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Plugin metadata hydration is pre-existing; once installed entries hydrate, MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery must complete its new per-entry directory validation and the existing format/manifest reads before marketplace plugins become available. If the customization marketplace service is instantiated, plugin installation records also remain checking until their new directory validations settle. Watch registration itself is asynchronous and not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve every hydrated installed plugin URI and verify it is a directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serial resolve per installed marketplace plugin on each discovery refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The source list was created in memory; existing format detection and manifest reads happened afterward without this root-directory stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks publication of the marketplace discovery result and therefore the aggregate plugin list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register a non-recursive correlated watcher for each unique installed-plugin parent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: P watcher registrations, where P is the number of distinct parent URIs after grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No parent watchers were registered; per-plugin root/component watchers still existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registrations are started asynchronously and are not awaited, but retain provider watch resources for discovery lifetime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve candidate installation directories to verify persisted records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Usually one concurrent resolve per persisted plugin record; more only when the exact target is missing and multiple matching installed candidates exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reconciliation used only in-memory installed-plugin lookup and did not cross the filesystem boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Keeps each record in checking state until validation completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several probes/reads per newly built plugin entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same format detection and manifest reads occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already blocked discovery before the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch GitHub marketplace metadata on a persisted-cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sequential per unhydrated marketplace entry, with persisted/in-memory cache reuse where available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical hydration behavior existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Hydration must finish before entries appear in installedPlugins, but this path is not added or made more frequent by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N hydrated installed marketplace plugins, P unique parent directories (P <= N), and R persisted customization plugin records. Discovery performs N new root resolves serially; customization reconciliation normally performs one resolve per record concurrently, with extra candidates only for duplicate matching installations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery validates entries serially in its for loop. CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService uses Promise.all across records, so up to R file resolves can be in flight. Metadata hydration is pre-existing and sequential; parent watch setup has no explicit limiter but consists of P asynchronous registrations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Directory existence results are not cached, so cold and warm reconciliation repeat stats. Marketplace metadata has a persisted TTL cache and in-memory hydration behavior that pre-dates the diff. Watchers are rebuilt when installedPlugins changes; there is no negative directory cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new resolve calls, serial/concurrent scheduling, observable triggers, and watcher count are directly visible in the changed call paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical users likely have few installed plugins, and local filesystem stat cost is platform-dependent; very large installed sets are not established. The added calls and ordering are certain, but the expected startup delay is too uncertain/small to report separately.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. The diff adds bounded directory validation needed to reject stale targets; realistic cardinality and local-stat cost do not establish a separate actionable startup regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: External deletion or replacement of an installed marketplace plugin directory
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A new parent watcher detects the target event and a zero-delay RunOnceScheduler coalesces events before refreshing discovery. Refresh serially revalidates all installed entries; aggregate plugin publication can then trigger customization-record reconciliation and its filesystem checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive correlated filesystem changes and schedule discovery when a watched installed target is affected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One callback per relevant correlated watcher event; pending callbacks coalesce to one refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: External target deletion was not observed through a parent watch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts the refresh required to remove the deleted plugin from discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-resolve all installed target directories after the event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N serial resolves per coalesced refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The deleted plugin is not removed from the published list until this pass finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate recorded plugin directories after aggregate plugins changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Usually R concurrent resolves per aggregate list update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Record state was inferred from metadata only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Marketplace missing-state transitions wait for the corresponding stat.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N installed marketplace plugins, P grouped parent watchers, event burst size E, and R marketplace customization records. Scheduler coalesces an event burst into one discovery refresh while pending.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events for a pending refresh are coalesced by one RunOnceScheduler. The discovery refresh serializes N stats; subsequent customization record validation can issue up to R concurrent stats. There is no cross-refresh cancellation before work starts, but versioning suppresses stale publication.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No positive or negative existence cache is used; every scheduled refresh re-stats all hydrated installed entries. Parent watchers persist until the installed list changes or discovery is disposed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: parent grouping, event filtering, zero-delay scheduling, serial discovery, and concurrent record reconciliation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem providers may emit different event granularity, and installed-plugin counts vary, but scheduler coalescing and exact N/R scaling are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new work is the intended response to an infrequent external deletion, is coalesced per event burst, and remains bounded by installed/recorded plugins.

Scenarios.Scenario: Uninstall a discovered or customization-marketplace plugin
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The durable entry is removed immediately in memory and its installed.json write is delayed/off-path, but the new IPluginInstallService.uninstallPlugin promise now waits for source cleanup. UI actions and customization uninstall await that promise, so source existence checking, recursive deletion, and parent pruning must finish before the action reports completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check source existence, recursively delete the repository/package cache, then resolve and prune empty parent directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cleanup target per hydrated uninstall; recursive filesystem operations scale with all files in that target, followed by a bounded parent walk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: MarketplaceAgentPluginDiscovery launched the same best-effort cleanup without awaiting it and returned true immediately after removing the installed record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced onto the awaited UI uninstall critical path; this is the reported regression.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One throttled write after installed-store changes, with changes within 100 ms coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Removing an installed entry already scheduled the same persisted-store write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the uninstall critical path because set schedules the write without awaiting it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Size and file count of the unique git repository or npm/pip cache selected for cleanup, directory depth to the cache root, and the number of remaining descriptors checked for shared ownership. Relative-path/shared sources can skip deletion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One uninstall runs cleanup serially: shared-target scan, exists, recursive delete, then serial parent resolve/delete. Independent user actions have no shared cleanup limiter, though normal UI use is typically one action at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cleanup cache exists. Remaining descriptors prevent deletion when another installed plugin has the same cleanup target. A unique source is fully deleted; an unhydrated entry skips cleanup because metadata is unavailable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed await, recursive cleanup implementation, and both awaited UI callers were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact deletion time varies with platform, antivirus/indexing, and cache size; large repositories and package dependency trees make multi-second delays realistic. The critical-path movement itself is unambiguous.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported a medium-severity cleanup-lifecycle latency regression anchored to the new await.

Scenarios.Scenario: Plugin manifest update and exact target removal during an existing discovery session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing root/manifest watchers invoke readManifest. The diff adds a root resolve before existing format detection and manifest reading; FILE_NOT_FOUND now triggers a complete discovery refresh. Manifest-only updates pay one extra root stat before content can update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the plugin root before detecting format and rereading the manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new root resolve per relevant manifest callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The callback went directly to format detection and manifest reading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one async stat before publishing a manifest update; on missing roots it initiates the intended full refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several existing probes/reads per manifest callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already formed the manifest-update critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Frequency of relevant manifest watcher events for one plugin; a missing root additionally causes a full refresh over N marketplace entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Watcher callbacks can invoke async readManifest without an explicit per-plugin sequencer; discovery refresh versioning prevents stale publication. Normal manifest edits are isolated to the affected plugin.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No stat cache or event coalescer is used inside readManifest. Existing derived component observables and watchers retain plugin entries between full refreshes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the extra resolve is directly added at the start of the watcher callback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Watcher event frequency depends on editor/save behavior and filesystem provider; one local stat per relevant manifest event is usually small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is a bounded single-stat cost that enables reliable directory disappearance handling and does not establish meaningful user-visible degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remove a stale durable entry whose marketplace metadata cannot hydrate
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Customization uninstall falls back to IPluginInstallService, which removes the exact durable URI. Because no hydrated plugin object exists, source cleanup is skipped; only in-memory filtering and the delayed installed.json write occur.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist removal from installed.json after the 100 ms write delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced write for the store mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The storage mechanism existed, but callers lacked the new exact-URI uninstall route for an unhydrated entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off-path; uninstallPlugin returns after scheduling because no hydrated source cleanup runs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N durable installed entries scanned/filtered once; serialized installed.json size grows with N.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in-memory scan/filter followed by one throttled asynchronous storage write; no cleanup subprocess or recursive delete is started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This is the negative metadata-hydration case. The implementation intentionally distinguishes an existing durable URI from the hydrated installedPlugins observable and does not create shadow metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the installed lookup is absent, cleanup branch is skipped, and removeInstalledPlugin schedules the existing store write.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed entry counts are expected to be small; no evidence supports costly serialization at realistic N.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new stale-entry path is bounded and avoids expensive cleanup when metadata is unavailable.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files. Reported one introduced latency regression: best-effort recursive source-cache cleanup is now awaited by user-visible uninstall actions. Also traced startup discovery, customization record reconciliation, external target deletion, watcher lifetime, manifest refresh, and unhydrated-entry removal; their added filesystem work is bounded or necessary at realistic plugin counts and did not meet the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
